text: The original attention divides the query‑key dot products by √dₖ (i.e., scales them) before the softmax because without scaling the dot products can become large in magnitude when dₖ is large, pushing the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Scaling by 1/√dₖ mitigates this effect and stabilizes training. [C:attention:9] [C:attention:10]

Moshi’s Depth Transformer is built with 6 identical layers and uses a model dimension of 1024 [C:moshi:41].

The smoothing module is introduced to turn the discrete chunk‑boundary decisions into differentiable, interpolated representations, thereby restoring gradient flow that is blocked by the discrete nature of chunk boundaries and enabling stable training dynamics[C:dynchunk:22]. It is shown to be essential for maintaining stable training; without it, compression‑ratio fluctuations occur[C:dynchunk:65].

The hierarchical network consists of three stages: (i) a small encoder network that processes the raw data, (ii) a main network that operates on compressed chunks, and (iii) a decoder network that upsamples and processes the data at the original resolution[C:dynchunk:6].

Moshi’s Inner Monologue method generates text tokens as a prefix before producing audio tokens.  It extends hierarchical semantic‑to‑acoustic token generation by first predicting time‑aligned text tokens, which are then used to guide the subsequent generation of speech tokens from a neural audio codec.  This prefix‑text step improves linguistic quality and enables streaming speech‑recognition and text‑to‑speech while keeping inference latency low[C:moshi:1].
